description: A quantizer for a scale you build yourself: the input voltage is spread evenly over the tones switched on in the matrix and sent out as 1V per octave

Chooses how many octaves of the matrix are used: 5 uses all five, 3 uses the three in the middle, and 1 uses octave 0 alone
Sets the probability used when random is triggered, 0 at the counter-clockwise end and 1 at the clockwise end
Switches every tone in the matrix off and clears every candidate mark
Adds 0 to 11 half tones to the tone picked from the matrix, without changing which tone was picked
Chooses what a random trigger does to each tone it considers: latch switches that tone on at probability p and off otherwise, and toggle flips it at probability p

inputs.text: The voltage to be quantised, spread evenly over the tones switched on in the matrix; it is read as 0V to 10V and anything outside that is clamped to it
A pitch here names the matrix tone that a trigger at toggle switches, read as 1V per octave with 0V naming the C of octave 0; the base offset is not applied to it
A trigger here switches the matrix tone named by the voltage at the v/oct input; channel by channel, each trigger switches the tone named by the same channel there
A trigger here switches every tone in the matrix off and clears every candidate mark
A trigger here re-rolls every tone that is switched on or marked as a candidate, each one at the probability set by p
Adds to the p knob, 0.1 of probability per volt, and the sum is held between 0 and 1
Adds to the base knob, 1.1 half tones per volt; the sum is clamped to 0 to 11 half tones and cut down to a whole one

outputs.text: The picked tone as 1V per octave, with the base offset added; the C of octave 0 is 0V
A 10V pulse 1ms long each time the tone at the v/oct output changes

notes: nothing comes out until a cable is patched into in and at least one tone in the matrix is switched on. With no tone on, the v/oct and change outputs hold whatever they last carried.
the matrix is five octaves of twelve half tones, the octaves numbered -2 to 2 across the panel and the half tones rising up each column. The C of octave 0 is 0V at the v/oct output.
a matrix lamp is green for a tone switched on, blue for the tone being picked now, and yellow for a candidate. A lamp is dim where its tone falls outside the octaves oct range is using.
a tone that a random trigger switches off is left marked as a candidate, so a later random trigger can bring it back. Switching a tone by hand or through the toggle input clears that mark.
with no tone switched on and no candidate marked, a random trigger treats all sixty tones as candidates, and it always leaves at least one tone switched on.
the in jack is polyphonic: each channel is quantised against the same scale and gets its own pulse at change. The random, reset, p and base cv inputs are read from their first channel only.
menu: bipolar input — reads the in jack as -5V to 5V rather than 0V to 10V, by adding 5V to the voltage before it is spread over the tones
